RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r1.claim: Rāzī says يوم is most plainly governed by what follows: on the day they are pushed, they are told that this is the fire they denied.
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r1.anchor: الظاهر أنه منصوب بما بعده وهو ما يدل عليه قوله تعالى : { هاذه النار } ( الطور : 14 ) تقديره يوم يدعون يقال لهم هذه النار

RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, يوم can be an appositive for the day in 52:11, the day the deniers are promised and punished.
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r2.anchor: ويحتمل غير هذا وهو أن يكون يوم بدلا عن يوم في يومئذ تقريره فويل يومئذ للمكذبين ويوم يوعدون

RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r3.claim: The wording conveys the terror of Hell: its keepers do not approach it, but shove and cast its inmates in from a distance.
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r3.anchor: قوله { يدعون إلى النار } يدل على هول نار جهنم ، لأن خزنتها لا يقربون منها وإنما يدفعون أهلها إليها من بعيد

RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r4.claim: Using the verbal noun دعّ presents the shove as a real and undeniable push, like insisting that a trivial blow or weak run does not merit its name.
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r4.anchor: الإيذان بأن الدع دع معتبر يقال له دع ولا يقال فيه ليس بدع

RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r5.speaker: قارئ
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r5.claim: On the reading دعاء, the word is an accusative circumstantial expression: they are called to the fire as people summoned to it.
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r5.anchor: إلا على قراءة من قرأ { يدعون إلى نار جهنم * دعاء } فإن دعاء حينئذ يكون منصوبا على الحال

RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r6.claim: The description of being pushed toward Hell appears to conflict with 54:48, which says they are dragged through the fire.
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r6.anchor: وقال تعالى : { يوم يسحبون فى النار } ( القمر : 48 ) نقول الجواب عنه من وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r7.claim: One reconciliation is that angels drag them through one fire and then, from a distance, cast them into a distinct, hotter Hell; 40:71–72 describes dragging through boiling liquid before kindling in the fire.
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r7.anchor: يسحبونهم في النار ثم إذا قربوا من نار مخصوصة هي نار جهنم يقذفونهم فيها من بعيد

RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r8.claim: A second reconciliation assigns different stages or tasks to different angels: one pushes them toward the fire and another drags them within it.
RAZI-FULL:v28p211#2/r8.anchor: جاز أن يكون في كل زمان يتولى أمرهم ملائكة ، فإلى النار يدفعهم ملك وفي النار يسحبهم آخر

RAZI-FULL:v28p212/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p212/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p212/r1.claim: A third reconciliation is that chains let them be dragged within the fire while the one pulling them remains outside.
RAZI-FULL:v28p212/r1.anchor: جاز أن يكون السحب بسلاسل يسحبون في النار والساحب خارج النار

RAZI-FULL:v28p212/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p212/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p212/r2.claim: A fourth possibility is that angels push them into Hell in humiliation, then enter it themselves and drag them through it.
RAZI-FULL:v28p212/r2.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون الملائكة يدفعون أهل النار إلى النار إهانة واستخفافا بهم ، ثم يدخلون معهم النار ويسحبونهم فيها

STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r1.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r1.claim: Commentators agree that al-Ṭūr is Makkan, most likely from the latter half of the Makkan period.
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r1.anchor: commentators agree that al-Ṭūr is from the Makkan period, most likely from the latter half.

STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r2.claim: Some say Sūrah al-Ṭūr was revealed immediately after Sūrah 32, al-Sajdah.
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r2.anchor: According to some it was revealed immediately after Sūrah 32, al-Sajdah.

STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r3.claim: The sūrah is named for the Mount mentioned in its first verse; most understand al-Ṭūr as Mount Sinai wherever it appears in the Quran, while the full name occurs in 23:20 and 95:2.
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r3.anchor: name from the mention of the Mount

STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r4.claim: The opening half follows Sūrah 51 by treating the promised Day (51:60) and punishment for its wrongdoers and disbelievers (51:59–60); the sūrah affirms that promise (51:5, 51:22) and further warns of it.
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r4.anchor: the first half (vv. 1–28) focuses upon the subject of the concluding verse of that sūrah, the Day that they are promised (51:60

STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r5.claim: The sūrah begins with oaths and the coming punishment and Judgment, contrasts the deniers' fate with the reverent's reward, answers accusations against the Prophet, challenges deniers, and ends by counseling patience and praise of God.
STUDYQURAN:52:intro/r5.anchor: Al-Ṭūr begins with a series of oaths and a promise of God’s impending punishment and the Day of Judgment (vv. 1–10)

STUDYQURAN:52:12/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:52:12/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:52:12/r7.claim: The deniers are graphically described as violently cast into Hell, dragged on their faces, shackled, and given boiling liquid and cold, murky fluid.
STUDYQURAN:52:12/r7.anchor: The violent way the deniers are cast into the Fire is described graphically in many verses: they are dragged upon their faces (54:48)

STUDYQURAN:52:12/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:52:12/r8.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:52:12/r8.claim: An alternative reading says they are called unto Hell with a great calling.
STUDYQURAN:52:12/r8.anchor: This verse could also be read, “a day when they are called unto the Fire of Hell with a [great] calling” (Bḍ).

TAB-FULL:v21p576/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p576/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v21p576/r2.claim: Qatada says the deniers are driven toward Hell with force.
TAB-FULL:v21p576/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا} [الطور: 13] قال: «يزعجون إليها إزعاجا»

TAB-FULL:v21p576/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p576/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v21p576/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the pushing as driving and coercion.

TAB-FULL:v21p576/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p576/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v21p576/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says they are pushed, comparing the verb to the rebuke and harsh treatment of an orphan.
TAB-FULL:v21p576/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قول الله

BURSEVI:v9p155#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p155#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p155#2/r14.claim: Daʿʿ is forceful pushing; the expression evokes pushing a stumbling person and then driving the condemned violently toward Hell.
BURSEVI:v9p155#2/r14.anchor: الدع الدفع الشديد وأصله أن يقال للعاثر دع دع

BURSEVI:v9p155#2/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p155#2/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p155#2/r15.claim: They are driven with hands bound to their necks and forelocks pulled to their feet, pushed into the Fire on their faces or backs.
BURSEVI:v9p155#2/r15.anchor: بأن تغل أيديهم إلى أعناقهم وتجمع نواصيهم إلى أقدامهم فيدفعون إلى النار دفعا على وجوههم وفي أقفيتهم

BURSEVI:v9p155#2/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p155#2/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p155#2/r16.claim: Yawm may be an apposition to the day the sky heaves, or a time adjunct for an understood statement introducing the next verse.
BURSEVI:v9p155#2/r16.anchor: ويوم إما بدل من يوم تمور أو ظرف لقول مقدر قبل قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:52:11-15/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:52:11-15/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:52:11-15/r7.claim: The verb for driving means to push forcefully, and the day phrase explains “that day” in the preceding verse.

TABRISI:52:9-16/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:52:9-16/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:52:9-16/r10.claim: They are violently and harshly shoved toward Hell.
TABRISI:52:9-16/r10.anchor: أي دفعا بعنف وجفوة قال مقاتل:

TABRISI:52:9-16/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:52:9-16/r11.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:52:9-16/r11.claim: Maqatil says their hands are bound to their necks, forelocks gathered to their feet, and they are shoved face-first into Hell.
TABRISI:52:9-16/r11.anchor: قال مقاتل: هو أن تغل أيديهم إلى أعناقهم وتجمع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r1.claim: The phrase يوم يدعون is an appositive for يومئذ.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda defines الدع as a harsh, forceful shove and cites the Qur'anic description of someone shoving an orphan in 107:2.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة (¬1): دععت (¬2) في قفاه, أي دفعت, ومنه قوله: {يدع اليتيم} [الماعون: 2]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r3.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r3.claim: Al-Layth cites a poem in which people push an orphan during famine as evidence for the sense of الدع.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r3.anchor: وأنشد الليث: إذا القوم في المحل دعوا اليتيما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r4.speaker: عامة المفسرين وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r4.claim: The general exegetes say they are driven into the Fire face-first; Qatada describes them as being violently hurried there.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r4.anchor: قال عامة المفسرين: يدفعون إلى النار دفعا على وجوههم (¬4)، وقال قتادة: يزعجون إليها إزعاجا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r5.speaker: مجاهد وابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r5.claim: Mujahid describes them as shoved from behind, and Ibn al-A'rabi glosses الدفر as pushing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: دفرا في أقفيتهم (¬6). قال ابن الأعرابي: الدفر: الدفع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r6.claim: Muqatil says their hands are shackled to their necks and their forelocks tied to their feet behind them before they are pushed face-first into Hell.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p483#3/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل: يغلون أيديهم إلى أعناقهم، وتجمع نواصيهم إلى أقدامهم وراء ظهورهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:52:12-15/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:52:12-15/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:52:12-15/r2.claim: They are shoved toward Hell with a forceful, violent push.

QASHANI:52:11-13/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:52:11-13/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:52:11-13/r3.claim: The verb means that they are driven and dragged violently.
QASHANI:52:11-13/r3.anchor: { يوم يدعون } أي: يجرون ويسحبون بالعنف

QASHANI:52:11-13/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:52:11-13/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:52:11-13/r4.claim: Hell signifies deprivation and pain in the depth of rebellious nature, amid chains of attachments and bodily dispositions.
QASHANI:52:11-13/r4.anchor: في قعر بئر الطبيعة الفاسقة المنحوسة في سلاسل التعلقات

ELMALILI:52:1-16/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:52:1-16/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:52:1-16/r22.claim: The deniers are forcibly shoved toward Hellfire.
ELMALILI:52:1-16/r22.anchor: Cehennem ateşine bir kakılış kakılacakları gün

ELMALILI:52:1-16/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:52:1-16/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:52:1-16/r23.claim: This yawm either replaces the preceding yawm or is accusative under an implied saying, explaining the woe.

ITQAN:v2p331#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p331#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p331#2/r3.claim: Yudaʿʿun means they are pushed or driven forcefully.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p423#12/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p423#12/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p423#12/r1.claim: Yudaʿʿūna means they are pushed; the verb daʿa/adda means to push, as in 107:2 about pushing away an orphan.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p423#12/r1.anchor: {يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا} أي يدفعون. يقال: دععته أدعه دعا؛ أي دفعته. ومنه: {الذي يدع اليتيم} (1) .

MAJAZ:v2p231/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p231/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p231/r1.claim: Yudaʿʿūn means they are pushed; Arabs say daʿa fī qafāhu for pushing someone at the nape, as in 2:107. He notes a light form of yadaʿʿu al-yatīm.
MAJAZ:v2p231/r1.anchor: أي يدفعون، يقال: دعت فى قفاه أي دفعت

MAJAZ:v2p231/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p231/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p231/r2.claim: The phrase is compressed; its full form is fa-yuqālu hādhihi al-nār, then it is said: this is the Fire.
MAJAZ:v2p231/r2.anchor: «دعا هذه النار» (13- 14) مختصر مخرجه: فيقال: هذه النار..

NAHHAS:v4p253/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p253/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p253/r18.claim: يوم is accusative as an apposition to يومئذ.
NAHHAS:v4p253/r18.anchor: نصب يوم على البدل من يومئذ

NAHHAS:v4p253/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p253/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p253/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they are pushed by their necks until they reach the Fire.
NAHHAS:v4p253/r19.anchor: وروى قابوس عن أبيه عن ابن عباس ( يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا ) قال

SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r1.claim: يوم may be an adverb for an implied يقال with هذه النار, or an apposition to يوم تمور or the preceding يومئذ.
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون ظرفا ل " يقال " المقدرة مع قوله: " هذه النار " أي: يقال لهم هذه النار يوم يدعون.

SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r2.claim: The common form, with open dāl and doubled ʿayn, derives from دفع: they are shoved in the chest forcefully.
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r2.anchor: فتح الدال وتشديد العين من دعه يدعه أي: دفعه في صدره بعنف وشدة.

SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r3.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r3.claim: Al-Raghib says the root began as دع دع, a call to a stumbling person; the author considers this far from the sense here.
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r3.anchor: قال الراغب: " وأصله أن يقال للعاثر: دع دع، كما يقال له: لعا " وهذا بعيد

SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r4.speaker: علي والسلمي وأبو رجاء وزيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r4.claim: Ali, al-Sulami, Abu Raja, and Zayd ibn Ali read with quiescent dāl and light ʿayn, from دعاء: they are called to the Fire and told to enter.
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r4.anchor: وقرأ علي والسلمي وأبو رجاء وزيد بن علي بسكون الدال وتخفيف العين مفتوحة من الدعاء

SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r5.claim: هذه النار is a nominal clause governed by an implied saying verb: the guardians tell them, This is the Fire.
SAMIN-DURR:52:13/r5.anchor: و " هذه النار " جملة منصوبة بقول مضمر أي: تقول لهم الخزنة: هذه النار.

ZAJJAJ:v5p62/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p62/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p62/r2.claim: They are driven and pushed violently toward Hell; the same verb describes pushing an orphan away from what is due to him.
ZAJJAJ:v5p62/r2.anchor: ومن هذا قوله: (الذي يدع اليتيم)، أي يدفعه عما يجب له

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r4.claim: The author prefers coercive, harsh pushing with rebuke over merely withholding an orphan's right: in 52:13 the deniers are thrust into Hell despite having no right being denied.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p504/r4.anchor: ولاحق فيها للمكذبين يُدَعُّون عنه ويدفعون، وإنما الدعُّ سَزْقٌ بقهرٍ ونهرٍ وغلظة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r1.claim: Islahi says this exegesis seeks to prevent Orientalist, Jewish, and extremist Shiite mischief, and that attentive readers will be protected from it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r1.anchor: People who will carefully read it, will inshā’Allāh remain protected from the mischief of the Orientalists, the Jews and extremist Shiites.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r2.claim: Islahi says the Qur’an’s present arrangement was set by God and His Prophet, and is based on religious philosophy and divine-law wisdom rather than history, as with the Torah and Gospel.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r2.anchor: The Qur’ ān we have today has been arranged by God and His Prophet (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r3.claim: He holds that all Qur’anic groups are linked and each sūrah is closely tied to its predecessor; changing its placement would create a void in meaning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r3.anchor: Every sūrah is so deeply linked to the previous one that a slight change in its placement will create void in the meanings.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r4.claim: Within each sūrah, verses cohere under a central theme; removing even one risks damaging the sequence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r4.anchor: all the verses of a sūrah are so closely connected to another that even if one verse is removed from its current place

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r5.claim: The established mutawātir reading is the one in the current muṣḥaf, and Islahi bases his verse and word interpretations on that reading.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r5.anchor: The conventional and mutawātir reading is the one written in this muṣḥaf which is in our hands today.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r6.claim: He interprets each verse and word through Arab usage, discourse context, and Qur’anic parallels, saying this leaves no doubt.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r6.anchor: the language of the Arabs, the context of the discourse and parallels of the Qur’ ān in such a manner that no doubt remains.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r7.claim: He argues that interpreting through other readings sacrifices the Qur’an’s eloquence, purpose, and wisdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p6/r7.anchor: interpreting the Qur’ān on the basis of other readings is only possible at the expense of sacrificing its eloquence, purpose and wisdom.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p9/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p9/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p9/r1.claim: As the group’s third sūrah, al-Ṭūr follows Qāf and al-Dhāriyāt, which establish resurrection and judgment through intellectual, historical, inward, and outward proofs; those works present reward and punishment together.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p9/r1.anchor: This is the third sūrah of this group.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p9/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p9/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p9/r3.claim: Verses 1–16 introduce a severe warning to obstinate Quraysh, adducing historical and universal facts, insisting punishment cannot be hastened or averted, then depicting Judgment and deniers’ fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p9/r3.anchor: a vivid picture of the Day of Judgement, with a brief description of the dreadful fate of those who had denied it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p18/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p18/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p18/r6.claim: The verb describes pushing someone forcefully and hatefully; the repeated verbal form further intensifies the force.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p18/r6.anchor: to push someone with full force and hatred

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p18/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p18/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p18/r7.claim: After their worldly pranks, they will be driven forcefully to Hell and told that this is the Fire they mocked and denied.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p18/r7.anchor: it will be said to them that this was the Hell they would make fun of and reject in the previous world.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p247#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p247#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p247#2/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses their being driven to Hell as being shoved there forcefully.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p247#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم ﴾ قال يزعجون إليها إزعاجا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r7.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r7.claim: Al-Ḥawfī parses يوم as accusative governed by دافع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r8.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r8.claim: Makkī says واقع cannot govern يوم but gives no argument for the restriction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r8.anchor: وقال مكي: لا يعمل فيه واقع، ولم يذكر دليل المنع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r9.claim: Another parse makes يوم depend on لواقع, with ما له من دافع parenthetically interrupting the governor and its complement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو منصوب بقوله: لواقع، وينبغي أن يكون ما له من دافع على هذا جملة اعتراض بين العامل والمعمول.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r16.claim: Hell's keepers shackle disbelievers' hands to their necks, bring their forelocks to their feet, and drive them face-first into the Fire, thrusting them from behind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r16.anchor: يوم يدعون، وذلك أن خزنة جهنم يغلون أيدي الكفار إلى أعناقهم، ويجمعون نواصيهم إلى أقدامهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r17.speaker: علي وأبو رجاء والسلمي وزيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r17.claim: ʿAlī, Abū Rajāʾ, al-Sulamī, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read يدعون with a still dāl and open ʿayn, from the root meaning to call; they are called to come to the Fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p568/r17.anchor: وقرأ علي وأبو رجاء والسلمي وزيد بن علي: يدعون، بسكون الدال وفتح العين: من الدعاء،

ALUSI-FULL:v27p30/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p30/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p30/r1.claim: The unbelievers are shoved violently toward the Fire, hands bound to necks and forelocks gathered to feet, then cast into it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p30/r1.anchor: أي يدفعون دفعا عنيفا شديدا بأن تغل أيديهم إلى أعناقهم وتجمع نواصيهم إلى أقدامهم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p30/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p30/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي والسلمي أبو رجاء
ALUSI-FULL:v27p30/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Ali and al-Sulami Abu Raja read with still dal and open ayn, from الدعاء, meaning they are called toward the Fire; daʿʿan is circumstantial.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p30/r2.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي والسلمي أبو رجار ( يدعون ) بسكون الدال وفتح العين من الدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p30/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p30/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p30/r3.claim: Yawm may be appositional to the day in 52:9 or a time adverb for the quoted divine speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p30/r3.anchor: بدل من يوم ( تمور ) أو ظرف لقولمحكي به قوله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p387#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p387#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p387#2/r3.claim: Yudʿaun means they are shoved forward, pushed harshly and roughly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p387#2/r3.anchor: دفعا بعنف وجفوة، وذلك أن خزنة جهنم يغلون أيديهم إلى أعناقهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p387#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p387#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p387#2/r4.claim: Hell's guards bind their hands to their necks, pull their forelocks to their feet, and drive them face-first into the Fire, prodding their backs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p387#2/r4.anchor: يغلون أيديهم إلى أعناقهم، ويجمعون نواصيهم إلى أقدامهم، ثم يدفعون بهم إلى النار دفعا على وجوههم

BAYDAWI-FULL:52:13/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:52:13/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:52:13/r1.claim: They are violently shoved toward Hell, with their hands bound to their necks and forelocks gathered to their feet as they are driven there.
BAYDAWI-FULL:52:13/r1.anchor: يدفعون إليها دفعا بعنف، وذلك بأن تغل

BAYDAWI-FULL:52:13/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:52:13/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:52:13/r2.claim: A reading takes yadʿūn from ‘calling’; then daʿʿan describes them as being summoned.
BAYDAWI-FULL:52:13/r2.anchor: من الدعاء فيكون دعا حالا بمعنى مدعوين

BAYDAWI-FULL:52:13/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:52:13/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:52:13/r3.claim: Yawm is either an appositive to the earlier yawm tamūru or a time adverbial for an implied statement being narrated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:52:13/r3.anchor: يوم } بدل من { يوم تمور } أو ظرف

BIQAI-FULL:v7p295/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p295/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p295/r5.claim: They are driven harshly and forcefully toward Hell by whatever agents God appoints; repeating the root as دعًّا intensifies and confirms the image.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p295/r5.anchor: أي يدفعون دفعا عنيفا بجفوة وغلظة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p295/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p295/r6.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p295/r6.claim: Al-Baghawi describes Hell’s keepers raising the sinners’ hands to their necks, gathering their forelocks to their feet, then thrusting them face-first and shoving them from behind.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p295/r6.anchor: قال البغوي : وذلك أن خزنة جهنم يعلون أيديهم إلى أعناقهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p295/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p295/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p295/r7.claim: Hell is portrayed as a grimacing, loathing, coarse, roaring layer that receives them.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p295/r7.anchor: وهي الطبقة التي تلقاهم بالعبوسة والكراهة والغليظ والزفير

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3315#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3315#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3315#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they are shoved by their necks until they are brought to the Fire.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3315#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم قال : يدفع في اعناقهم حتى يردوا النار .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p43/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p43/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p43/r1.claim: يوم يدعون is an inclusive apposition to يوم تمور السماء مورا in 52:9.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p43/r1.anchor: { يوم يدعون } بدل من { يوم تمور السماء مورا } وهو بدل اشتمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p43/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p43/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p43/r2.claim: Daʿʿ means forceful pushing; it humiliates them and depicts frightened people falling back as the angels assigned to drive them to the Fire shove them forward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p43/r2.anchor: والدع : الدفع العنيف ، وذلك إهانة لهم وغلظة عليهم ، أي يوم يساقون إلى نار جهنم سوقا بدفع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p43/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p43/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p43/r3.claim: The verbal noun دعا intensifies يدعون and is indefinite to convey the action's magnitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p43/r3.anchor: وتأكيد { يدعون } ب { دعا } لتوصل إلى إفادة تعظيمه بتنكيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p186#2/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p186#2/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p186#2/r21.claim: The second yawm is an appositive to yawmidhin in the preceding verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p186#2/r21.anchor: و: يوم الثاني بدل من: يومئذ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p186#2/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p186#2/r22.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p186#2/r22.claim: Ibn Abbas explains yudʿawn as being driven by the neck with force, humiliation, and rough jostling; he links it to 107:2.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p186#2/r22.anchor: و: يدعون قال ابن عباس معناه: يدفعون في أعناقهم بشدة وإهانة وتعتعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p186#2/r24.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p186#2/r24.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p186#2/r24.claim: Abu Raja al-Ataridi reads the verb as a form of calling, with a still dāl and open ʿayn, rather than the usual forceful driving.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p186#2/r24.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء العطاردي: «يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم» من الدعاء بسكون الدال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p49/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p49/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p49/r1.claim: Ibn Qutaybah explains yudaʿʿūn as ‘they are pushed’; the same root appears in the description of one who repels an orphan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p49/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي يدفعون يقال دععته أدعه أي دفعته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p49/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p49/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p49/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they are shoved by their necks until they reach the Fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p49/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس يدفع في أعناقهم حتى يردوا النار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p49/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p49/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p49/r3.claim: Muqātil says their hands are chained to their necks and their forelocks gathered to their feet; they are pushed face-first toward Hell.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p49/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل تغل أيديهم إلى أعناقهم وتجمع نواصيهم إلى أقدامهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p430#3/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p430#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p430#3/r10.claim: The deniers are shoved and driven toward Hellfire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p430#3/r10.anchor: أي: يدفعون ويساقون، {إلى نار جهنم دعا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p430#3/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p430#3/r11.speaker: مجاهد، الشعبي، محمد بن كعب، الضحاك، السدي، الثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p430#3/r11.claim: These authorities explain the phrase as the deniers being thrust into the Fire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p430#3/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد، والشعبي، ومحمد بن كعب، والضحاك، والسدي، والثوري: يدفعون فيها دفعا

JISHUMI:v9p6609/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6609/r4.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v9p6609/r4.claim: The majority read with shadda, from forceful pushing; the author compares ṣakka yaṣukku ṣakkan.
JISHUMI:v9p6609/r4.anchor: قراءة العامة: (يدعون) بالتشديد من الدع، وهو الدفع بشدة، دعه يدعه دعا: إذا دفعه

JISHUMI:v9p6609/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6609/r5.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
JISHUMI:v9p6609/r5.claim: Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī reads lightly, from calling or summoning.
JISHUMI:v9p6609/r5.anchor: وعن أبي رجاء العطاردي: (يدعون) بالتخفيف، من الدعاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p379/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p379/r6.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك والسدي وابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p379/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd gloss the condemned as pushed violently toward Hell; a rajaz line illustrates the force.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p379/r6.anchor: قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك والسدي وابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p379/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p379/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p379/r7.claim: Qatada instead explains the verb as violently rousing or driving them onward.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p379/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p379/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p379/r8.claim: Mawardi suggests a third possibility: Hell's wardens call down curses on the condemned.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p379/r8.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : أن يدعهم زبانيتها بالدعاء عليهم .

MUJAHID:v2p625/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p625/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p625/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses their being thrust toward Hell as being driven there forcefully.
MUJAHID:v2p625/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا ﴾ قال يقول يدفعون إليها دفعا

MUQATIL:52:11-14/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:52:11-14/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:52:11-14/r2.claim: After judgment, Hell's keepers shackle disbelievers' hands to their necks, bind forelocks to feet behind their backs, and push them face-first into Hell, where they are told this is the fire they denied.
MUQATIL:52:11-14/r2.anchor: خزنة جهنم بعد الحساب يغلون بأيدى الكفار إلى أعناقهم، ثم يجمعون نواصيهم إلى أقدامهم، وراء ظهروهم، ثم يدفعونهم في جهنم دفعا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p183#13/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p183#13/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p183#13/r1.claim: Daʿʿ means a violent shove: the keepers bind their hands to their necks, gather forelocks to feet and drive them face-first or backward into the Fire.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p183#13/r1.anchor: والدع الدفع العنيف وذلك ان خزنة النار يغلون ايديهم إلى اعناقهم ويجمعون نواصيهم إلى اقدامهم ويدفعونهم إلى النار دفعا

QURTUBI-FULL:52:9-13/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:52:9-13/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:52:9-13/r18.claim: The day they are driven is an apposition to “that day” in 52:11.
QURTUBI-FULL:52:9-13/r18.anchor: قوله تعالى: { يوم يدعون } «يوم» بدل من يومئذ

QURTUBI-FULL:52:9-13/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:52:9-13/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:52:9-13/r19.claim: Yudaʿʿūna means they are violently shoved toward Hell; daʿa means to push, as in 107:2 about the one who pushes away an orphan.
QURTUBI-FULL:52:9-13/r19.anchor: «يدعون» معناه يدفعون إلى جهنم بشدة وعنف

QURTUBI-FULL:52:13-16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:52:13-16/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:52:13-16/r1.claim: A tafsīr account says Hell’s keepers bind their hands to their necks, gather their forelocks to their feet, and shove them face-first into the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:52:13-16/r1.anchor: وفي التفسير: إن خزنة جهنم يغلون أيديهم إلى أعناقهم، ويجمعون نواصيهم إلى أقدامهم، ثم يدفعونهم في النار دفعا على وجوههم

QURTUBI-FULL:52:13-16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:52:13-16/r2.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي وابن السميقع
QURTUBI-FULL:52:13-16/r2.claim: Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī and Ibn al-Sumayqa read the verb lightly, from “inviting”; when they approach, the keepers tell them the Fire they denied is before them.
QURTUBI-FULL:52:13-16/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء العطاردي وابن السميقع «يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا» بالتخفيف من الدعاء فإذا دنوا من النار قالت لهم الخزنة
